newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: FIGURE SKATING-ELDREDGE, STOJKO LOOK FOR BEST FORM.
newsitem.headline: FIGURE SKATING-ELDREDGE, STOJKO LOOK FOR BEST FORM.

text.p: American Todd Eldredge and Canadian Elvis Stojko, winners of the last three world titles, need to rediscover their very best form to hold off the rampant Russians this week.

Olympic and European champion Alexei Urmanov and former European champion Ilya Kulik showed their intent in Sunday's qualifying to end the run of four successive North American world championship men's triumphs this week.
They both completed huge quadruple jumps to overshadow the best efforts of Eldredge and Stojko, who must pull up their socks for the main event which opens on Wednesday with the short programme.
Title-holder Eldredge, nursing a sprained ankle, plunged to the ice landing a triple axel in the qualifying round while Stojko, the Canadian who won in 1994 and 1995, went down attempting his quad.
Fellow Canadian Kurt Browning won the 1993 title but the streak could end this week if Eldredge and Stojko cannot reproduce the form which earned them their reputations.

The Russians are hungry, Urmanov to fulfil the promise he showed when he was a surprising winner of the Olympic title in 1994, Kulik to add to his success in winning the European title on his debut in 1995.
There are other contenders, including 1996 European champion Viacheslav Zagorodniuk of Ukraine who does not have a quad but whose triple axel is superb.
Igor Pashkevitch, formerly of Russia but now skating for Azerbaijan, is also a threat and there will be a lot of attention on American newcomer Michael Weiss.

He was believed for a time to have done the first quad in competition by an American during the national championships last month, only for it to be ruled later that he had touched down with his trailing foot on landing.
The first title will be decided on Wednesday night when Germans Mandy Woetzel and Ingo Steuer also try to hold off the Russians in the freeskating section of the pairs.
They won the short programme on Tuesday night from the holders and European champions, Marina Eltsova and Andrei Bushkov, with two more Russians, Elena Berezhnaia and Anton Sikharulidze, third.

Americans Jenni Meno and Todd Sand hold fourth place ahead of compatriots Kyoko Ina and Jason Dungjen but a bigger threat to the leaders could come from Russian former champion Artur Dmitriev with new partner Oksana Kazakova.
